Because the text says these are three positions of the same die, mark physical faces and use the relative positions and orientations of the printed words to decide when a repeated word is the same physical face versus another face with the same word. Build a cube net from the three corner views: the consistent inventory of the six physical faces is three faces labelled 'YES', two faces labelled 'no', and one face labelled 'maybe'. Since a fair die has six equally likely faces, the probability of landing on a 'YES' face is 3/6 = 1/2.

method.method_draft: Constraint/enumeration method. Enumerate the 24 possible rotations of a cube and impose that three of those rotations reproduce the three observed views, including which label is on the top/left/right visible face and the orientation of the word on that face. The satisfying labeling gives exactly three of the six physical faces labelled 'YES'. Therefore the favorable outcomes are 3 out of 6, so the probability is 1/2.
